pushback_verification: All 12 verified against the committed tree before any edit. Confirmed independently rather than relayed: the arc doc's only `R-crc-10` IS the counted list entry, so the endpoint marker would break its own input (finding 1); `orbit/specs/orbit-architecture-engine/spec.md` does state that rulings are engine-opaque, and this change declared no MODIFIED capabilities (finding 2); both literal review-marker tokens were present and the discovery grep in /orbit:address-reviews is raw with no inertness rule (finding 3); the resolver really is project-local then user-global then package (finding 7); the declared exclusions really yield 54/52 and not the 50/48 this change had written (finding 11). ONE DOWNGRADE NOTE, recorded not suppressed: finding 6's project-local template path is forward-looking — `git ls-files 'orbit/schemas/*'` returns zero today, so the exclusion gap breaks nothing currently; the table was still promising a category it did not cover. Entries below are generated FROM the external findings file, so titles and files are byte-identical to the pass they resolve.

resolutions.title: The ruling-count source is dogfooded as a different fact and can invalidate its own input
resolutions.action: RATIFIED OPTION A (chat). Endpoint marking is REVERSED — a decision this change made two rounds ago and that this finding correctly killed. The dogfood now marks a ruling COUNT inside a written current-state sentence, never the range endpoint, in `CLAUDE.md` (which holds no rulings index, so it is safe by construction). The general rule is now NORMATIVE in the spec with its own scenario: a marked span SHALL NOT sit inside the text its own source is computed from. Design D3 records the reversal and the trap (the arc doc's only `R-crc-10` IS the counted entry; marking it breaks that entry's bold span and drops the count to 9), and notes that count-as-endpoint was unsound anyway since the two coincide only while ids stay contiguous. The architecture doc's own current-state sentence moves to task 5.4 as an ARCHITECT recommendation — apply marks nothing there.

resolutions.title: Inline-code inertness is not specified to an implementable grammar
resolutions.action: Added a CLOSED six-row inline-code table to the spec (equal-length run closes; different-length run does not; an unmatched run is literal text and the region stays LIVE; a span crossing a line ending is one region; adjacent spans leave live text between them; a run inside a fence is not a code span), with the explicit statement that the mask is computed over the WHOLE DOCUMENT before marker scanning — a streaming toggle cannot decide the unmatched-run case without lookahead. Task 2.2 and the Touchpoints now require an ADDITIVE mask and PROHIBIT modifying `FenceTracker.inFence`/`handle`, which the trail and report parsers share. The reviewer's scope estimate — tens of lines plus tests once the boundary is explicit — is what makes this a specification fix rather than a redesign.

resolutions.title: The JSON contract cannot represent required error kinds or summary validity
resolutions.action: Replaced D5b's flat record with a DISCRIMINATED schema keyed on `kind`: `registry` (registry file + detail, no line/source/span), `marker` (file + line + detail, no span or value), `unknown-source` (file + line + source, no value), `mismatch` (all five fields). Added a spec scenario requiring every failure kind to be representable with exactly its own fields and no null padding. Validity now uses the bulk validator's existing shape — a `sources` entry in `byType` rolled into `summary.totals` — so a non-zero exit can never report zero failed items, and a `--sources`-only run carries only the `sources` key. Task 3.2 carries both.

resolutions.title: `schema.version` has an unnamed environment-dependent input
resolutions.action: SETTLED UNDER R-crc-3 and named for reversal. `schema.version` resolves PROJECT-LOCAL then PACKAGE BUILT-IN and SKIPS the user-global override tier, because that tier lives in a developer's data directory and honouring it would make the same checkout emit different values on different machines — a marked repository fact would become machine-dependent. The spec states the tier in the source table and in prose as an R-crc-10 input that is NAMED rather than inherited; design D3's table agrees; task 1.2 requires a test that a global override does not change the emitted value. THIS FINDING WAS MISSED BY MY OWN TRIAGE and appeared in neither the obvious-fix preview nor the decision lane; it was caught while applying and is recorded here rather than quietly folded in.

resolutions.title: Registry source names can be valid yet impossible to reference
resolutions.action: Requirement 1 now requires registry source names to match the marker NAME grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`, so an entry can no longer parse, resolve and appear in coverage while being unreferenceable. Declared parameter values must be non-empty strings (a YAML number, null or list is a clean error naming entry and parameter), and a `doc` or `schema` parameter naming something that does not exist is a clean validation error rather than a silently absent source. Task 1.3 enumerates all three.
